does.text: Only queues. It appends a copy of the incoming eoc::itemwall::CreateWallRequest (0x88 bytes each) to the system's own dynamic array and does nothing else; no component is touched here. That a spell's CreateWall functor calls it is a guess from the name; no caller was read.

does.text: Update and CreateWalls have the same body. When the queue is non-empty and a query (ECS query slot, index in a global, contents not resolved) has no matching entity, each queued request becomes a new entity via a deferred EntityCommandBuffer::CreateEntity. That entity gets two components added: ls::SavegameComponent (an empty one-byte component, so the wall is saved) and esv::itemwall::CreateComponent, filled from the request (position/direction values, a FixedString, a SpellId, and a 16-byte tail) plus an embedded CreateWallResult returned by eoc::itemwall::CreateWall (the template-based geometry/entity computation, a separate function). The queue is then destroyed and emptied every call.
